33. MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS

General population = 1/330.

FX = 80%.

Sibling affected = 10%.

1 parent affected = 10%.

Monozygotic = 20%.

Dizygotic = 5%.

Recurrence after 1 affected child = 27%

 

⇨Chronic inflammatory demyelinating disorder.
⇨Genetic screening difficult (HLA – DR31*1501).

Risk Factors:

•Viral infection EBV.
•Smoking.
•Obesity.

Types:

•Relapsing, Remitting MS RRMS 80%.
•P0 Progressive PPMS 10 – 15%.
•Sec0 progressive SPMS.

 

⇨Expanded Disability scale.

EDS – for monitoring of disease progression – 20-point score. 0.5 increment with each score.

O – normal, 10 – death due to MS.

 

⇨Clinical Presentation:

Common:

-Fatigue.
-Urinary incontinence.
-Numbness/ tingling.
-Loss of balance.
-Dizziness/ vertigo.
-Visual problems.
-Pain
→Acute.
→Chronic.
-Spasticity
-Cognitive symptoms.
-Mood changes.

Less common:

-Dysarthria
-Dysphonia.
-Dysphagia
-seizures
-Termers
-Breathing problems.
-Itching.
-Headache.
-Hearing loss.

II0 Symptoms:

-Recurrent UTI.
-Poor postural alignment.
-Loss of BMD.

Effect of Pregnancy & B.F on MS:

•Fewer relapses and lower progression (Most relapses in 1st and 2nd ).
•Predictor of relapse – pre-pregnancy relapse rate.
•A/N immunosuppression => spontaneous remission.
•New relapse => new symptoms.
•Painful visual loss => optic neuritis => new relapse.
•New symptoms => prompt review by MDT.
•Pseudo relapse => flare up of all symptoms with greater intensity.
•B.F => reduce relapse 4-fold.

B.F => L.H => prolactin => anovulation => TNFα=> CD4 cells.

Effects of MS on Pregnancy:

•AMH low in MS.
•Voluntary childlessness (22% vs 13%).
•Women choose TOP (20% vs 12%).
•Sexual dysfunction 30 – 70%.
•More C/S.
•More instrumental delivery => more neuromuscular weakness.

Fetal Effects:

Increased risk

1.PTB (8 vs 6%

2-LBW

3-IUGR (1.7 times)

No effects on

Miscarriages

Still birth

anomalies

Drug safety and category:

-Disease modifying therapy (DMT).
⇨Glatiramer acetate (b) & interferon (c) => relatively safe to use.
-Stop after conception.
-C/I in pregnancy.
⇨Steroids © can be given in pregnancy.
⇨Natalizumab ©. Alemtuzumab ©, SGA risk.
-Stop before conception.
-Contraction for 2-3 months in Natalizumab and 4 months in Alemtuzumab
⇨Teriflunomide x CI.
⇨FINGOLOMID x (CI) + 2m0CC – risk of miscarriage.
⇨Mitoxametrone (D), 6m0 CC, ovarian reserve
⇨Methotrexate (x) 6m0 CC.
⇨Mycophenolate (D), 6 weeks CC.
⇨Dimethyl Fumarate ©, can stop cc immediately. Short half time.
⇨cladribine (D), 6m0 CC.

Pre – pregnancy counselling:

•MDT:
-Neurologist.
-Nurse specialist.
•MS not a hereditary.
•Stop smoking => disease progression by smoking.

ANC:

•MDT:
•Rest, Avoid stress, fiber diet, physiotherapy.
•Amitriptyline, Diazepam for pain & spasticity respectively.
•Monthly mid-stream urine.
•DVT prophylaxis if immobile.

Anaesthesia:

•Safe – pethidine, TENS, NO, regional.
•Growth scans – recommended.
•MRI for relapses.

Treatment of relapses:

-Oral I/V steroids.
-Monitor GDM & HTN while on steroids.
-Stress dose steroids during labour/ delivery.

I/P Care:

NVD => safe.

-Planned C/S in women with neurological problems.
-Higher EDSS => IOL.
-OVD => maternal exhaustion/ fatigue.

P/P Care:

-B.F
-DMT => avoid B.F or B.F after 4 hours of drugs.
-All CC => safe.

MS & ART:

-More relapses after ART 17-Fold.
-3m0 after ART due to Agonist protocol and after un – successful trials.
